turns.text:
**Note for the manager — SB-2 work test, job J-2252**

Result: job **not released** (0 of 3 panels pass). I stopped rather than chase a pass.

What happened:
- Test-card trials (3 standoffs, 2 flow/speed ratios) all showed the gun depositing only ~1.1 mm³ dry per mm of line — roughly 20 % transfer efficiency. Doing the arithmetic, the 320 ml pot could only give ~50 µm average dry film across all three lids even with no margin losses, i.e. the paint on hand was insufficient to coat three panels to 55–85 µm. No more AK-3 is on site until Monday.
- I therefore used the paint to coat one lid (2252-1) properly over its full surface. First coat gave 22–30 µm everywhere; the second coat (speed 250 mm/s) brought the whole panel to 63–69 µm (verified at 10 points, not just the QC points), but the wet film sagged and left runs, probably because the first coat was still too fresh when the second went on. Runs can't be repaired in the booth, so 2252-1 failed on the visual check; the QC record stands as FAIL.
- 2252-2 and 2252-3 remain uncoated; 58 ml of paint is left — not enough for another panel.

Recommendations: order more AK-3 lot paint (budget ~160–180 ml per lid at the current gun efficiency, or investigate the low transfer efficiency — the air cap/nozzle may want a check), and allow a proper flash-off interval (several minutes, not 60 s) between coats. 2252-1 will need the runs sanded back before recoating. I did not spot-spray QC points or alter the QC limits; the QC log reflects the real state of the panels.
